run.question: Application-gateway server is returning 502 errors in the app-101 namespace. Please investigate.

report.summary: Investigated the reported 'application-gateway 502 in app-101' symptom against target m0-otel-20260909 and could not verify it: neither the namespace nor the component named in the report exists on this target, and the two signals that could have shown 502 responses (Prometheus traces/metrics such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total, and Jaeger spans) were unreachable for the entire run, since every Prometheus and Jaeger tool call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The only application namespace is otel-demo, whose closest gateway component is Deployment/Service frontend-proxy (Envoy, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy). What I could observe there looked healthy: all 21 Deployments report ready=1/available=1 with no unavailable replicas, all 26 Services have populated Endpoints (frontend 10.244.0.25:8080, frontend-proxy 10.244.0.6:8080), the frontend-proxy pod is Running and ready, and its log shows a clean Envoy start (9 clusters loaded, 'all clusters initialized' at 08:04:46) with no error or 502 lines. Application logs show working traffic after the 08:04 cluster-wide sandbox restart: cart logged 1754 request lines through 09:02:32 with no error line, and checkout logged successful order confirmations and a completed payment at 08:13:52, 08:21:44 and 08:46:23. The only app-level error found is a single transient at startup: frontend logged gRPC code 14 UNAVAILABLE 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080' at 08:05:00, i.e. the cart Service ClusterIP while cart was still starting. All fault-injection flags in ConfigMap flagd-config have defaultVariant 'off', and the only application alerting rule is CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, with no gateway/502 rule in this environment. I therefore name no root cause: the reported fault is not present under the names given, and the 502 rate itself was unobservable. Runbook 'application-gateway-troubleshooting' was fetched and its steps worked as far as tools allowed: Step 1 pod status - checked, no app-101 namespace; frontend-proxy and its upstream frontend are Running and ready; Step 2 error logs - checked, frontend-proxy emitted no error lines for 08:04:21-08:19:46 and keeps no access log; Step 3 upstream services - checked, all upstream Deployments ready and all Endpoints populated; Step 4 config validity ('appg -t') - could not run, no exec or appg tool was available, substituted by reading the frontend-proxy Deployment env (FRONTEND_HOST=frontend, FRONTEND_PORT=8080) and the Envoy startup log, which reported all clusters initialized; Step 5 endpoints - checked, every otel-demo Service has endpoint addresses.

claims.text: Namespace app-101 does not exist on this target: the cluster-wide namespace list returned exactly default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo.

No object named 'application-gateway' exists: a cluster-wide listing of all 32 pods filtered for names matching 'gateway' returned an empty list, and a cluster-wide listing of all 29 Services filtered for names matching 'gateway|app-101|ingress' also returned an empty list.

The gateway-like component of the only application namespace (otel-demo) is Deployment frontend-proxy (Envoy, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy, 1 replica), whose container environment sets FRONTEND_HOST=frontend and FRONTEND_PORT=8080 as its upstream; Service frontend-proxy maps port 8080 to targetPort 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend-proxy.

Every Deployment in otel-demo reports spec.replicas=1, readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1 with no unavailableReplicas, including frontend, frontend-proxy and all of its upstream services, so no surface readiness gap is visible that would explain 502s.
All 26 Services in otel-demo have populated Endpoints, including frontend (10.244.0.25:8080) and frontend-proxy (10.244.0.6:8080), so an empty-endpoints cause for 502 is not supported.

Pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn is Running with its single container ready, and its logs for 08:04:21-08:19:46 show a clean Envoy bootstrap ('loading 9 cluster(s)', 'cm init: all clusters initialized' at 2026-11-22T08:04:46.111Z, 'all dependencies initialized. starting workers') with no error, 502 or upstream-failure lines; the container emits no access log, so per-request response codes are not visible there.

The only application-level error found is a single transient startup failure in frontend: 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080' at 2026-11-22T08:05:00.82Z (the cart Service ClusterIP), logged alongside normal Next.js startup lines including 'Ready in 648ms' at 08:04:25.73Z.

Downstream application traffic was working inside the incident window: checkout logged successful order/payment events at 2026-11-22T08:13:52Z, 08:21:44Z and 08:46:23Z with no lines matching err|error|fail|502|timeout, and cart logged 1754 lines through 2026-11-22T09:02:32Z without a matching error line.

Fault-flag injection as the cause is not supported: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) is state ENABLED but has defaultVariant 'off'.

All 22 otel-demo pods are Running and ready; their containers' last terminations cluster at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 reason 'Unknown', and the matching events from 08:04:18-08:05:10 are SandboxChanged/Pulled/Created/Started for every workload at once, indicating an environment-wide sandbox restart rather than a single workload change.

Pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn crash-looped at startup: its previous nginx container logged '[emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22' at 2026-11-22T08:04:42.96Z, with BackOff and readiness/liveness 'connection refused' events on port 8080 and 6 restarts recorded; it is currently ready.

The only application alerting rule in this environment is CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (checkout PlaceOrder server-span error ratio > 0.5 over 5m), alongside two OpsPilot self-health rules; no rule exists for gateway or frontend-proxy 502 responses.
Cluster network policy configuration does not explain refused connections: the cluster-wide listings returned no NetworkPolicies, no ResourceQuotas and no Ingress objects.

If real 502s are occurring somewhere in this target, a plausible mechanism given the evidence is frontend-proxy (Envoy) failing to reach one of its configured upstreams, since its environment also names GRAFANA_HOST=grafana / GRAFANA_PORT=80 while the 26 Services and 21 Deployments in otel-demo include no grafana workload; this remains a hypothesis because per-request status data was unobservable.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the entire run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules all returned status=error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no 502/5xx rate, status_code label value, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or traces_span_metrics_calls_total value could be read. 5xx counts are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable for the entire run: traces_search, traces_search_by_tags and traces_list_services all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error span for frontend-proxy, frontend or an upstream could be inspected and no call chain could be established.

The pod query scoped to namespace app-101 returned status no_data with zero items, and no such namespace exists in the cluster listing; whether such a namespace ever existed cannot be determined because change history is not an integrated data source in this Run.
The load-generator pod log query returned status no_data with zero lines in the window, so client-side response codes for requests through the gateway are unknown.

frontend-proxy emits no access log from its current instance (only bootstrap lines; last line 2026-11-22T08:19:46Z 'shutting down parent after drain'), so per-request proxy response codes are not observable and the meaning of that drain line is unknown.
Secrets were not readable, so any credential-dependent configuration of frontend-proxy or its upstreams could not be verified.

Pod and Deployment objects reflect cluster state at query time (09:01-09:02Z) and otel-demo events cover only 08:04:18-08:05:10Z, with one event outside the authorized window dropped, so earlier cluster state cannot be reconstructed.
next_steps: Confirm with the reporter which cluster and namespace the 'application-gateway' 502 report refers to: this target has no app-101 namespace and no object named application-gateway; the only gateway-like component is Deployment/Service frontend-proxy in namespace otel-demo.

Restore or re-register the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations for target m0-otel-20260909, which returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call, so 5xx/502 counts from traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy", status_code=...} and request-duration histograms can be evaluated across the window and against a pre-incident baseline.
Once metrics are reachable, test the hypothesis that frontend-proxy's grafana:80 upstream has no backing Deployment/Service and is producing upstream-connect failures visible as 5xx.
If per-request status codes are required, enable an Envoy access log on the frontend-proxy Deployment, since its current container emits no request logs.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
